notes:
Pashalik of Timbuktu (Arma), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row, but the bamana-empire dossier already names `pashalik-of-timbuktu` as a counterpart for its 1748/1752/1769 steps, hence this slug. Pages: Pashalik of Timbuktu, Arma people, Timbuktu, Massina Empire (re-read in the fix).

Revised 2026-10-19 after the review (verdict fail). (a) Start moved from 1591 to 1618 (c2): the Pashalik page's infobox calls 1591-1621 a 'Moroccan Governorate' and Sultan Moulay Zidan 'relinquished direct control over the Sudan territories in 1618'; saadi-sultanate holds Timbuktu and Gao (gain 1591/5), Djenné (gain 1592) and records the pashalik as its vassal from 1618, so the two dossiers no longer double-claim about 83,000 km2. 1591-1617, kept here instead of the ledger: the Saadian army left Marrakesh on 16 October 1590, won at Tondibi in March 1591, occupied Gao and took Timbuktu on 30 May 1591 (the official capital), conquered Djenné in 1592; scholars of Timbuktu were executed or exiled in 1593 (Timbuktu page); 'after 1612' the pashas were appointed locally by the Arma. The infobox's other dates, 1612 and 1621, are the alternatives for the start. (b) Djenné drops out in 1818 (loss cp massina-empire, c2). (c) I disagree with the review on Timbuktu in 1826: the Massina Empire page (opened 2026-10-19) says Massina 'in 1826/7 conquered Timbuktu' but lists the Arma pashas of Tomboctou among its vassals and 'firmly' controlled the town only in 1833 'when a Fulbe governor was appointed'; the pashalik therefore keeps Timbuktu to 1833 and the infobox end (1833) stands. massina-empire (not mine) draws Timbuktu from 1826 as an outright gain and should record vassal_start 1826 / vassal_end 1833 cp pashalik-of-timbuktu. (d) Bamana: bamana-empire's 1748 gain, 1752 loss and 1769 gain of Timbuktu (cp pashalik-of-timbuktu) are left unanswered here: the Pashalik page is silent on the Bambara, the Biton Coulibaly page has Bamana hold Timbuktu 'only briefly' without a year and the Ngolo Diarra page puts firm control of Djenné and Timbuktu between 1766 and 1790, undated; a Cliopatria Bamana shape reaches the Timbuktu disc in 1748-1751 and 1800-1819 (25 and 68 of 206 cells) and the Djenné disc from 1713 (65 of 148 cells) - those overlaps are for the bamana-empire owner (af-03-a) to settle. Other options not taken: ending the state in 1737, when 'the rule of the Arma over Timbuktu' ended (page body); the infobox gives Tuareg tributary 1787-1833 and Moroccan vassal 1621-1826. The Tuareg tribute of 1787 has no dossier (no Tuareg state). Gazetteer: Tondibi, Timbuktu, Gao, Djenné are all in the gazetteer. The three discs are not an outline: the Mali admin-1 regions of Timbuktu and Gao are too large.
